_readme: The restructure map for scripts/doc_claims.py: an explicit, reviewed entry
per known restructure, so a historical cite that was true when written
resolves to where the thing lives NOW instead of erroring against the
current tree. Loaded by load_restructure_map(); a structurally broken map
aborts the scan (exit 2) rather than silently running without it.
Schema -- every path entry is keyed by the CITED token (no line number)
and carries exactly one of:
targets : [paths...]  present-check. A path ending in '/' is a PACKAGE,
present while any indexed file lives under it. mode 'all'
(default) requires every target; mode 'any' requires one.
untracked : [repo paths]  the listed paths must NOT be in the HEAD tree
(the promise a doc row makes about purged or never-built
files); a recommitted file fails the cite that called it gone.
external : true  the cite names code outside this repository (installed
packages); existence is not machine-checkable from the tree,
and the entry is printed as RESTRUCTURED on every run so the
honest gap stays visible instead of silent.
Every path entry also requires 'cites_in': the backend/docs/ file(s)
whose historical rows the entry was written for. A claim is resolved
only when it is MADE IN one of those files; the same bare token cited
in any other doc falls through to the plain tree lookup, so an entry
cannot silently green unrelated prose (token-keyed false pass).
Every entry requires a 'reason' of at least 24 characters: the reason is
what the RESTRUCTURED log line prints, so an unexplained pass is a
validation error, not a quiet one.
Test entries map a historical test name to its shipped successor
('successor'); the pass requires the SUCCESSOR to exist, so deleting the
replacement fails the old cite again. Test entries are deliberately NOT
scoped by cites_in: a def name is a unique identifier and a rename keeps
its referent wherever the old name is quoted.
Precedence: for a cite that has an entry scoped to the citing file, THE
MAP DECIDES -- it preempts the direct index lookup, any counter-example
directive on the line, and the numeric line check. path_line cites
resolved through the map are downgraded to warnings: the location is
verified, the historical line number is not, and the log says exactly
that.
To extend: add one entry, then run
python scripts/doc_claims.py --base 84c8fa71164c23f1a955c67cfc71bd324545519f
python -m unittest discover -s scripts -p "test_*.py"
The unit suite validates this file's shape and that every targets/successor
still resolves, so a map entry that rots is red in CI, not just at night.

orders/views.py.reason: flat orders/views.py was split into the orders/views/ package (VIEWS-SPLIT: __init__, checkout, payment, refund, return, order, admin); a line number from the flat file has no meaning inside a package, so path_line cites resolve the package and carry a line-check warning

backend/orders/views.py.reason: the repo-root-qualified cite of the same flat module (see the orders/views.py entry); both cite forms resolve to the views package and must fail the day the package is deleted

views.py.reason: bare views.py cites span the orders monolith prose, products (changes row 44), accounts (section-20 MFA) and the shipping skeleton; append-only history cannot say which app each line meant, so the claim is resolved existentially over this explicit list and fails when the last listed views module is gone

urls.py.reason: bare urls.py cites span the config root router, accounts refresh/logout prose, the orders refund row and the shipping skeleton; no single file is pinnable from append-only history, so the claim passes while any listed urls module exists

tests.py.reason: bare tests.py cites are mostly .coveragerc globs (*/tests.py) and app-generic references, never one app's file; existential over every tests.py in the tree so the claim dies only when the last one does

serializers.py.reason: bare serializers.py cites belong to the shipping app-skeleton rows and the B07 returns rows, i.e. more than one app; existential over this explicit list

admin.py.reason: bare admin.py cites span orders, the shipping app-skeleton rows and the SPEC-18-1 products row; existential over this explicit list rather than guessed per line

models.py.reason: bare models.py cites are orders-machine prose (changes Black/coverage rows, spec-run-state B07a COD lines) plus app-generic mentions; existential over this explicit list

apps.py.reason: the only bare apps.py cite is the shipping app-skeleton row in changes (the file list a new shipping app needs), and shipping/apps.py exists, so this is pinned strict

__init__.py.reason: the only bare __init__.py cite is the same shipping app-skeleton row, pinned strict to the package marker that row was asking for

migrations/0001_initial.py.reason: the only bare cite is the shipping app-skeleton row naming the initial migration a new app needs; shipping/migrations/0001_initial.py exists, so pinned strict

commands/__init__.py.reason: the only cite is the changes row that created the repo's first management-command package under products; pinned strict to that package marker

views.py/urls.py.reason: slash-joined accounts cite from the LogoutView row ('verified against views.py/urls.py'); both accounts files must exist for the verification the row describes to have happened

models.py/admin.py/views.py.reason: slash-joined orders cite from the state-machine consolidation row: ADMIN_FULFILMENT_NEXT was consolidated verbatim from these three homes, so all three must still exist

admin.py/views.py.reason: slash-joined orders cite from the consolidation row where admin and views import the machine from orders.state; both homes must still exist

accounts/urls.py.reason: the S20 compliance row cites the mfa route block at lines 59-75; the ruff reformat (b6e887c) compacted the file after that was written and the mfa/* routes now sit at 42-48 of a 49-line file, so the location is verified and the historical line numbers are not (cite refresh is a separate task)

products/management/commands/seed_demo.p.reason: the SPEC-14-1 row cites this as a PENDING proposal, a command nobody has written; it must stay out of the tree until that row is rewritten, so building it first fails this entry on purpose

loadtest.py.reason: the spec-run-state hygiene note (2026-09-30) names this scratch file as purged and gitignored and forbids committing it; the entry checks that promise in both plausible locations instead of demanding the file exist

red_team_probe.py.reason: same hygiene note; backend/red_team_probe.py was tracked once (c07e139) and purged, so both plausible locations must stay out of the HEAD tree

django/contrib/admin/options.py.reason: Django's own source, installed as a package and outside this repository; the scanner indexes only repo files (stdlib-only by design per the nightly header), so the cite is recorded as external and printed every run rather than silently passed

coverage.py.reason: test-gaps cites the coverage TOOL as a gate name, not a repository path; it is an installed dependency the tree index never contains, so the cite is recorded as external and printed every run

iews.py.reason: byte-eaten head of views.py at c873b27, quoted as corruption evidence; the intact cite's home is the restructured orders/views/ package, so the fragment resolves there and dies with it

ests_returns.py.reason: byte-eaten head of tests_returns.py at c873b27, quoted as corruption evidence; the intact file still exists and this entry pins the fragment to it

handlers/base.py.reason: the TIER1-launch ENVELOPE-WIRE backlog row's bare cite is Django's OWN django/core/handlers/base.py (the request-handler entry that renders the DRF response before ErrorEnvelopeMiddleware can rewrite it), installed in site-packages and outside this repository; recorded external like django/contrib/admin/options.py so the fully qualified location lives in this reason and the cite prints every run instead of passing silently

test_the_gate_reads_no_clock_at_all.reason: B07d inverted the tripwire and the changelog records 'It is replaced by' the successor, which asserts the inverse on the same gate

test_the_gate_reads_the_window_on_every_.reason: the changelog's BUG-2 row recorded this spelling as never shipped ('the shipped method is') and corrected the row to the successor's name

test_the_projection_reveals_nothing_the_.reason: renamed in B07b cycle 2 because the old name oversold the check (changelog: 'RENAMED this cycle from')

test_no_field_is_writable.reason: the changelog quotes this name in ellipsis truncation; the shipped pin's full def is the successor and no shorter name of its own ever existed

test_failed_verify_appends_no_event.reason: renamed in b5581f9 (SPEC-10-04) when a failed verify began appending the payment-failed event; the diff replaces one def with the other in one hunk

test_customer_totp_field_ignored.reason: SPEC-20-10 rewrote the pin when the storefront stopped serving a totp field (changelog: 'is now test_customer_door_has_no_totp_field')

test_webhooks_prefix_reserved_until_webh.reason: SPEC-1-06 replaced the absence pin with the endpoint pin it had been waiting for (changelog: 'It is now')

test_checkout_requires_authentication_an.reason: renamed in 0d9c438 (B04 guest checkout removed the auth requirement); the diff replaces one def with the other and the cart gate is kept

test_slug_overflow_without_collision_cur.reason: feaee45 (PG-2b) fixed the clamp and replaced this bug-documenting pin with the truncation pin for the same no-collision scenario

test_confirmation_send_is_registered_not.reason: renamed in 05cd9f4 (TIER1-ASYNC-CONVERT) when verify_payment stopped registering an inline send and began writing the NotificationOutbox row; the diff replaces one def with the other in orders/tests.py and the docstrings swap the pinned defect for the converted contract

test_verify_success_sends_confirmation_e.reason: renamed in 05cd9f4 (TIER1-ASYNC-CONVERT) when the browser verify began enqueueing the order.paid confirmation for the drain worker instead of sending it; the diff replaces one def with the other in one hunk of tests/test_notifications.py

test_send_failure_does_not_break_the_pay.reason: renamed in 05cd9f4 (TIER1-ASYNC-CONVERT): the never-raise payment pin moved from SMTP-503 dispatch failure to outbox enqueue failure and the diff replaces one def with the other in tests/test_notifications.py; the separate request-path pin 05cd9f4 added to orders/tests.py has a different name and is not this cite's successor

test_a_stolen_email_and_key_buy_the_atta.reason: 7e63658 deleted this def from backend/orders/tests_guest.py with the guest-creation machinery it exercised (anonymous checkout is refused before the email or the key is ever read), and the shipped successor pins the same leak closed for an anonymous keyed replay

test_the_trailing_space_variant_of_a_sto.reason: 7e63658 removed the canonicalisation path this variant pinned because guest checkout is refused (a trailing-space address is never stored and never resolves to an owner); the whitespace-casefold guest_email survives only as one of the byte-identical refusal reasons the successor pins

test_a_keyed_replay_with_a_drifted_paylo.reason: 7e63658 deleted this def together with the keyed guest-agreement 409 it pinned: the guest keyed path is gone because anonymous checkout is refused before the Idempotency-Key is read, and the successor refuses an anonymous keyed replay outright

test_a_collapse_never_hands_back_the_cre.reason: 7e63658 removed the guest collapse this invariant guarded (no collapse can occur: anonymous checkout is refused and mints nothing), and the successor pins the same no-credential property on the refusal body, asserting guest_token is absent from the response

test_a_keyed_guest_resubmission_collapse.reason: 7e63658 deleted this def with the keyed guest resubmission machinery it pinned (guest checkout is refused uniformly, so no guest resubmission can collapse onto a first order), and the successor pins that an anonymous keyed replay reaches no order

test_an_over_length_guest_email_is_refus.reason: 7e63658 removed the guest-side email length gate this pin held because anonymous checkout is refused before any validation could write; over-length guest_email is now one of the byte-identical refusal reasons the successor pins across the guest reasons

test_an_over_length_shipping_field_is_re.reason: 7e63658 deleted this two-path def: the guest half died with guest creation (anonymous submissions get the uniform refusal, pinned inside the refusal class) and the account half was re-pinned under this successor, whose docstring records the width gate is an account gate now

test_the_guest_email_is_stored_in_one_ca.reason: 7e63658 removed the canonical guest_email storage this pin asserted because guest checkout is refused and no guest address is ever stored; the whitespace-casefold address survives only as a refusal reason, pinned byte-identical by the successor

test_a_case_variant_of_the_guest_email_i.reason: 7e63658 removed the guest owner resolver this consequence pin depended on (no guest owner exists to double, since anonymous checkout is refused), and the casefold-variant guest_email survives only as a byte-identical refusal reason the successor pins

test_an_identical_resubmission_collapses.reason: 7e63658 removed the unkeyed guest collapse this pin asserted because anonymous checkout is refused before idempotency is considered, so a resubmission mints nothing; the successor pins that a refused submission creates no order row, reservation or trail

test_verify_without_session_cookie_skips.reason: TIER1-WEBHOOK-CARCH renamed this def in place in backend/orders/tests.py: the old pin asserted a cookie-less verify left the cart full, which is the exact bug the Cart.order link closes; the successor keeps the same cookie-less scenario and pins the order-linked clear, and the TIER1-WEBHOOK-CARCH changelog row records the supersession
